stages.name: Indigenous nations
stages.desc: No European colony: the land is governed by its Native nations

stages.name: Spanish, French, Dutch or Swedish
stages.desc: A colony or mission of another European power

stages.name: English claim on paper
stages.desc: Granted by an English charter but not settled; still Indigenous land

stages.name: Proprietary colony
stages.desc: Owned and governed by a lord or a group of proprietors under a royal charter

stages.name: Self-governing colony
stages.desc: Settlers elect their own governors under a company or royal charter

stages.name: Royal colony
stages.desc: Ruled for the Crown by a governor the king appoints

states.name: Montana
timeline: Plains and mountain nations

states.name: North Dakota
timeline: Mandan and Hidatsa towns on the Missouri

states.name: Minnesota
timeline: Dakota and Ojibwe homelands

states.name: Michigan
timeline: Odawa, Ojibwe and Potawatomi homelands; French traders on the lakes
Cadillac founds the French post of Detroit

states.name: Ohio
timeline: Erie and other nations; much of it emptied by the Iroquois wars of the 1650s

states.name: Pennsylvania
timeline: Lenape and Susquehannock homeland
New Sweden's governor builds his seat on Tinicum Island
The Dutch conquer New Sweden
The Delaware settlements pass to the Duke of York
Charles II grants Pennsylvania to William Penn
Penn lays out Philadelphia

states.name: New York
timeline: New Netherland: New Amsterdam on Manhattan and Fort Orange up the Hudson
An English fleet takes New Amsterdam; it becomes the Duke of York's New York
A Dutch fleet retakes the colony
Returned to England by treaty
The duke becomes King James II: New York is a royal colony
Jacob Leisler seizes power after the revolution in England

states.name: Vermont
timeline: Western Abenaki homeland; French and English traders pass along Lake Champlain

states.name: New Hampshire
timeline: Fishing settlements at Strawbery Banke and Dover under Captain John Mason's grant
The New Hampshire towns join Massachusetts Bay
Separated from Massachusetts as a royal province
Part of the Dominion of New England

states.name: Maine
timeline: English fishing posts on paper grants in the Wabanaki homeland; French Acadia to the east
A royal charter makes Maine the province of Sir Ferdinando Gorges
Massachusetts Bay takes over the Maine settlements
Absorbed into the Dominion of New England under Sir Edmund Andros
Boston's revolt restores the old government
Part of the royal Province of Massachusetts Bay

states.name: Arizona
timeline: Hopi, O'odham, Apache and Navajo homelands; a few Spanish friars among the Hopi

states.name: New Mexico
timeline: Spanish New Mexico, ruled from Santa Fe over the Pueblo towns
The Pueblo Revolt drives the Spanish out
Diego de Vargas leads the Spanish back

states.name: Texas
timeline: Caddo, Karankawa, Apache and other nations; a short-lived French fort (1685) and Spanish missions (1690)

states.name: Louisiana
timeline: Caddo, Natchez, Houma and Chitimacha homelands
La Salle reaches the mouth of the Mississippi and claims Louisiana for France
Iberville enters the Mississippi: French Louisiana begins

states.name: Mississippi
timeline: Choctaw, Chickasaw and Natchez homelands
Inside Carolina's 1665 charter, which runs from sea to sea
The French build Fort Maurepas on Biloxi Bay

states.name: Alabama
timeline: Muscogee (Creek), Choctaw and Alabama towns
Inside Carolina's 1665 charter, which runs from sea to sea
French Louisiana founds Mobile

states.name: Florida
timeline: Spanish Florida: St Augustine and the missions of Timucua and Apalachee
Carolina's second charter claims land down to 29° north, beyond St Augustine
Spain begins the stone fortress of St Augustine
Carolina's governor besieges St Augustine and burns the town
Carolina's raid destroys the Apalachee missions

states.name: Georgia
timeline: The Guale missions of Spanish Florida line the coast
Carolina's second charter claims this coast too
Spain pulls its missions south after raids; the coast is Carolina's on paper only

states.name: South Carolina
timeline: Claimed on paper by Heath's patent; Kiawah, Edisto and other Cusabo peoples on the coast
Within Carolina's charter; Spain still claims the coast
English settlers from Barbados and England found Charles Town on the Ashley River
Charles Town moves to Oyster Point, today's Charleston
The proprietors suspend the Fundamental Constitutions
A last version of the Constitutions is drafted, then shelved; rice and slavery reshape the colony

states.name: North Carolina
timeline: Claimed on paper by Sir Robert Heath's patent of 1629; Tuscarora, Chowanoke and Algonquian towns
Charles II grants Carolina to eight Lords Proprietors, among them Lord Ashley
Albemarle, settled from Virginia, gets its first governor, William Drummond
The Fundamental Constitutions, drafted with Locke, are sent out; never put fully in force
Culpeper's Rebellion: settlers depose the proprietors' deputy
The proprietors suspend the Fundamental Constitutions

states.name: Virginia
timeline: A royal colony since 1624; tobacco plantations along the James and York rivers
Opechancanough leads the last great Powhatan war against the colony
Bacon's Rebellion: Jamestown is burned
James Blair founds the College of William & Mary
Governor Andros is allowed to resign after the Board of Trade, Locke among them, takes up Blair's complaints
The capital moves to Williamsburg

states.name: Washington
timeline: Within Maryland's charter; the Nacotchtank town on the Anacostia
Part of proprietary Maryland
Part of royal Maryland

states.name: Maryland
timeline: Charles I grants Maryland to Lord Baltimore; Piscataway and Susquehannock lands
The first settlers land at St Mary's
The Toleration Act protects all Christians who believe in the Trinity
A Protestant association overthrows the Catholic proprietor's government
Maryland becomes a royal colony

states.name: Delaware
timeline: The Dutch post of Zwaanendael is destroyed; Lenape homeland
New Sweden builds Fort Christina
The Dutch take New Sweden
Taken by the English for the Duke of York
Granted to William Penn as the Lower Counties
The Lower Counties meet in an assembly of their own

states.name: New Jersey
timeline: Part of New Netherland; Lenape homeland
The Duke of York grants New Jersey to Lord Berkeley and Sir George Carteret
Briefly Dutch again
Proprietary again; soon divided into East and West Jersey
The proprietors surrender government: a royal colony

states.name: Connecticut
timeline: Pequot, Mohegan and other Native towns; Dutch traders on the river
Puritan settlers found Hartford and govern themselves
A royal charter confirms Connecticut's self-government
Absorbed into the Dominion of New England
The charter government returns

states.name: Rhode Island
timeline: Narragansett and Wampanoag homeland
Roger Williams, banished from Massachusetts, founds Providence
A royal charter guarantees self-government and liberty of conscience
Absorbed into the Dominion of New England
The charter government returns

states.name: Massachusetts
timeline: The Massachusetts Bay Company governs Boston under its own charter; Plymouth lies to the south
King Philip's War devastates Native and English towns alike
The Crown annuls the Massachusetts charter
The Dominion of New England is ruled from Boston by Sir Edmund Andros
Boston rises against Andros and restores its old government
A new charter: a royal governor for the Province of Massachusetts Bay

states.name: Utah
timeline: Ute, Paiute and Shoshone homelands

states.name: Wyoming
timeline: Shoshone and other Plains and mountain nations

states.name: Colorado
timeline: Ute and other mountain and Plains nations

states.name: South Dakota
timeline: Arikara, Dakota and other Plains nations

states.name: Nebraska
timeline: Pawnee, Omaha and Otoe homelands

states.name: Kansas
timeline: Kansa and Wichita homelands

states.name: Oklahoma
timeline: Wichita and Caddo homelands

states.name: Iowa
timeline: Ioway and other Plains and prairie nations

states.name: Missouri
timeline: Osage and Missouria homelands

states.name: Wisconsin
timeline: Ho-Chunk, Menominee and refugee nations; French traders and missionaries

states.name: Illinois
timeline: The Illinois Confederation's towns along the rivers
French priests found a mission at Cahokia

states.name: Kentucky
timeline: Hunting lands of the Shawnee, Cherokee and other nations

states.name: Arkansas
timeline: Quapaw and Caddo homelands

states.name: Tennessee
timeline: Cherokee, Chickasaw and Yuchi homelands
Inside Carolina's 1665 charter, which runs from sea to sea

states.name: West Virginia
timeline: Appalachian hunting lands; Virginia's traders begin to cross the mountains in the 1670s

states.name: Indiana
timeline: Miami and other nations of the Great Lakes

events.title: Zwaanendael destroyed
events.text: The Dutch whaling post at today's Lewes is wiped out after a quarrel with the Lenape; no settler survives.

events.title: St Mary's City
events.text: Lord Baltimore's first colonists, Catholic and Protestant, land in Maryland and found St Mary's.

events.title: Providence
events.text: Roger Williams, banished from Massachusetts for his views, founds Providence on land of the Narragansett.

events.title: Hartford
events.text: Thomas Hooker leads Puritan settlers from Massachusetts to the Connecticut River.

events.title: Mystic massacre
events.text: In the Pequot War, colonists and their Native allies burn the Pequot fort at Mystic, killing hundreds.

events.title: New Sweden
events.text: Swedish colonists build Fort Christina at today's Wilmington.

events.title: Powhatan war
events.text: Opechancanough leads a last great Powhatan attack on Virginia; he is captured and killed in 1646.

events.title: Maryland Toleration Act
events.text: Maryland's assembly protects every Christian who believes in the Trinity, but threatens death for denying it.

events.title: New Sweden falls
events.text: Peter Stuyvesant's Dutch force takes the Swedish forts on the Delaware.

events.title: Carolina granted
events.text: Charles II grants the land between Virginia and Spanish Florida to eight Lords Proprietors, Lord Ashley among them.

events.title: Rhode Island charter
events.text: A royal charter allows Rhode Island's colonists full liberty in matters of religion.

events.title: New York
events.text: An English fleet takes New Amsterdam without a fight; it is renamed for the Duke of York.

events.title: Cape Fear colony
events.text: Settlers from Barbados found a first Charles Town on the Cape Fear River; it is abandoned in 1667.

events.title: Charles Town
events.text: English and Barbadian settlers land at Albemarle Point on the Ashley River and found Charles Town.

events.title: The Bahamas
events.text: Charles II grants the Bahamas to Carolina's proprietors; in 1672 Locke invests in the Bahamas venture.

events.title: Castillo de San Marcos
events.text: Spain begins a stone fortress at St Augustine against the English colony to the north.

events.title: The Dutch return
events.text: A Dutch fleet retakes New York for fifteen months.

events.title: King Philip's War
events.text: Metacom's Wampanoag-led alliance fights New England's colonists; thousands die and captives are sold into slavery.

events.title: Bacon's Rebellion
events.text: Nathaniel Bacon's rebels attack Native villages, defy the governor and burn Jamestown.

events.title: Culpeper's Rebellion
events.text: Settlers in Albemarle jail the proprietors' deputy in a revolt over the tobacco duty.

events.title: Pueblo Revolt
events.text: Pueblo peoples rise together and drive the Spanish out of New Mexico for twelve years.

events.title: Oyster Point
events.text: Charles Town moves to the peninsula between the Ashley and Cooper rivers, today's Charleston.

events.title: Raid on Guale
events.text: Raiders allied to Carolina attack the Spanish mission on St Catherines Island; Spain soon pulls its missions south.

events.title: Philadelphia
events.text: William Penn lays out his 'city of brotherly love' on the Delaware.

events.title: La Salle
events.text: René-Robert de La Salle reaches the mouth of the Mississippi and claims its whole basin for France.

events.title: Stuarts Town
events.text: Spanish forces destroy the Scottish settlement of Stuarts Town at Port Royal.

events.title: Dominion of New England
events.text: James II merges the northern colonies into one dominion without elected assemblies.

events.title: Boston revolt
events.text: News of the revolution in England reaches Boston; the town rises and jails Governor Andros.

events.title: Leisler's Rebellion
events.text: Militia captain Jacob Leisler takes over New York in the name of William and Mary.

events.title: Schenectady
events.text: French and allied Native fighters burn Schenectady in King William's War.

events.title: Salem trials
events.text: Witchcraft trials at Salem end with nineteen people hanged.

events.title: William & Mary
events.text: James Blair obtains a royal charter for a college at Middle Plantation, Virginia.

events.title: Rice and slavery
events.text: Rice becomes Carolina's great crop, grown by enslaved Africans whose numbers soon rival the settlers'.

events.title: Andros resigns
events.text: Virginia's governor is allowed to resign after the Board of Trade, Locke among its members, hears James Blair's charges.

events.title: Fort Maurepas
events.text: French explorers under Iberville build a fort on Biloxi Bay: French Louisiana begins.

events.title: Williamsburg
events.text: After Jamestown's statehouse burns, Virginia moves its capital to Williamsburg.

events.title: Detroit
events.text: Antoine de la Mothe Cadillac founds a French fort on the strait between Lakes Huron and Erie.

events.title: Mobile
events.text: The French move the capital of Louisiana to a new fort on the Mobile River.

events.title: Siege of St Augustine
events.text: Carolina's governor James Moore burns St Augustine but cannot take its stone fortress.

events.title: Apalachee destroyed
events.text: Moore's raid destroys the Apalachee missions; thousands of Apalachee are killed, enslaved or driven away.

events.title: Deerfield raid
events.text: French and Native raiders attack Deerfield and march over a hundred captives to Canada.

chartNote: Share of the area of the present-day US states on the map, by who governed each in a given year. Regions are today's state boundaries, not colonial ones; a colony usually held only a coastal strip, so this is a simplification, and almost all the land, even inside English charters, remained Indigenous. Carolina's charters ran on paper from sea to sea.
chartTitle: Who governed the land, by area
